chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: Visiting pianists and the two baby grands
summary: Pianists from Baltimore and Washington came on weekends to play classical pieces on the two baby grands his father bought for the sun parlor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: he would have like -- outstanding piano players would come down from Philly, (inaudible). My mother had a second floor which was really a sun parlor. And in that room my father had bought him two baby grand pianos and it was locked together. And he'd have these different piano players come in (inaudible), like Paul Lamoar, from Baltimore, Washington -- like come down on the weekend and visit us.
Do you remember -- I know you were small boy then -- but do you remember any names?

No, I don't. I can't remember any of the names. I always wondered who these fellows were. I know they used to come like on the weekend for a visit. And like on a Saturday morning they'd have tea or coffee and they'd go up in the room and they'd close the door. And then you wouldn't hear anything for about ten or fifteen minutes. Then they would start off.

They wouldn't come out. They wouldn't I'd know let me in there -- I was little -- because (inaudible) what they were doing. And they would be going over these different classic piano concerto things. They'd be doing that on the weekend.
